inputs.prompt:
A single uninterrupted fifteen-second HORIZONTAL 16:9 cinematic LIVE-ACTION continuation of Dante's Nevan guitar performance in the SAME opera stage. Begin at the supplied INITIAL FRAME, with the same young silver-haired human Dante, same open worn crimson leather coat, brown harness, dark trousers, fingerless black gloves and boots, and the exact same rigid asymmetric purple blade guitar. Preserve face, body proportions, cloth, all guitar blades and compact SHORT thick neck, string bed and apertures. One actor, one instrument. Real skin, individual hair, weighted leather, solid metal prop; no cartoon, plastic skin or game graphics. No costume redesign or instrument replacement.

INITIAL STATE AND CONTINUITY: This is the middle of an ONGOING solo immediately after the behind-the-head phrase and its return to the front. The first image IS the precise incoming waist-height guitar position, front three-quarter body, left boot forward, right boot behind, right wrist at strings, left glove on short upward-angled neck, low front-three-quarter camera and carved pillars/violet curtain/warm practical lights. Start with fingers, supporting knee, coat and camera already in motion. Complete the small weight transfer and the existing string stroke straight into the next phrase. No new establishing shot, testing note, musical intro, pose assembly, pause, teleport, costume reset or replay of the behind-head event. Keep the same screen direction, guitar scale, landmarks and warm/violet lighting.

CAMERA: Continue from the INITIAL FRAME's low front-three-quarter position without cutting. For the first two seconds preserve the incoming perspective and slow lateral drift. During the guitar's upward flourish, the camera physically retreats and tilts gently upward BEFORE the highest blade reaches the top, leaving visible free air around every tip. Track along the same audience-front hemisphere, revealing real pillar parallax. Maintain the actor, both hands, complete guitar and both boots in frame. Follow the kneeling descent by lowering modestly and retreating, preserving whole-body legibility; never zoom into the face or let camera movement substitute for body movement. No compensating full camera orbit, whip-pan, hidden cut, slow motion or static victory hold.

00:00-00:02: Continue the fast ongoing E-minor guitar phrase immediately. RIGHT glove makes clear alternating strokes at the actual compact string bed; LEFT fingers change notes on the same short neck. Dante completes the incoming step, settles into a wide grounded stance and shifts weight onto the rear boot. His eyes follow the neck and then rise with a small confident grin. Heavy coat and silver hair follow the body rather than anticipating it.
00:02-00:05.5: Keeping both original hand contacts, Dante sweeps the entire rigid Nevan UP and out through a broad diagonal arc in front and ABOVE his head, then down across the front to waist-height. This is the large overhead guitar flourish from the DMC3 performance, not another behind-head rest. The broad bladed body moves through visible empty air outside forehead, shoulders, arms and coat; blades never pass through flesh or fabric. Keep instrument length, thickness and three unequal blade tips unchanged even as its back becomes visible. A brief electrical filament follows a struck string; light does not conceal contact. Feet counterbalance the guitar's travel, knees flex, torso responds with weight and momentum. No throw, extra guitar, stretching, bending or levitation.
00:05.5-00:08: With the same Nevan now controlled IN FRONT, he pushes from a planted boot and performs ONE full grounded body turn using successive visible steps. We see his shoulder and back then his face returning toward the camera; this is his body turning, not a camera orbit. Both gloves retain the one solid guitar outside his body. The coat flares AFTER the torso and then follows the deceleration. End the turn balanced and still playing, not skating or jumping.
00:08-00:11: Dante drives a last fast front-facing solo phrase, knees wide and flexed, guitar neck angled upward. He leans back with supported hips and a grounded rear boot, then brings his center of mass forward again to prepare the landing. Right wrist continues physical string attacks, left fingers remain on the same compact neck. Grin gives way to a focused emphatic final phrase. No idle swaying to fill time.
00:11-00:13.5: He bends visibly through hips and knees, lowers onto BOTH knees and makes a SHORT controlled forward slide on the stage. Knee contact causes deceleration, coat settling and grounded body recovery; no instantaneous kneeling pose or travel through the floor. Strike ONE final ringing power chord as the descent reaches the floor. The guitar stays outside his chest and thighs, supported by the LEFT glove on its neck and the right hand during the strike. Show clear support throughout.
00:13.5-00:15: Recover from the kneeling landing into the iconic broad finishing flourish. The left hand supports Nevan diagonally along the left side, its lower body supported beside the left thigh; the RIGHT arm opens outward only AFTER the final string stroke. The guitar never floats, vanishes, clips through his knees or duplicates. Dante lifts his chest, breathes and looks forward with playful satisfaction while the final chord decays. Cloth, hair, fingers and camera continue to settle naturally through the last frame. Do not freeze the image or start another riff.

SOUND: Native synchronized diegetic electric guitar, continuing the same crunchy original E-minor rock solo around140BPM from the incoming take, with picked attacks aligned with the visible right-wrist strokes. Begin in the middle of the phrase, no fresh count-in or intro and no initial silence. Keep the same opera-chamber reverberation, close leather/boot/knee-contact sounds, and restrained electrical crackle after struck strings. The final sustained distorted chord rings and decays with room reflections during the finishing flourish. No copied game audio recording, added background score, voice, singing, band, drums, bass, applause, extra actor, microphone, captions, text or logo. No artificial audio fade or abrupt silence before the last frame.
